**"Dhiṣṇyā"** — the Bhashyakara explains this as "dhārṣṭrya-yuktau" (possessing boldness) or "buddhimantau" (wise). **Skandasvāmī derives it: "Dhiṣaṇā" means speech; her offspring, or the word "dhī" (insight) in its own feminine form, yields "dhiṣṇyā" — "those exceedingly wise, capable of grasping every matter."** Sayana's gloss — "courageous, wise" — is endorsed by Wilson. **Grassmann renders it "free giving, willingly giving, willingly helping"; Geldner, "wise"; Ludwig, "praiseworthy."** By a different word-family connection (from the root "dhī," to think), other commentators explain "Dhiṣṇyā" as "those that kindle the thoughts" — those who inspire the mind or speech. 1. **The rule and the objection.** By the Pāṇinian rule "vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam" (विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् — *vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣa-vacane bahuvacanam*, पा. ८-१-७४): when an earlier vocative that is a general term is followed by a plural vocative that is a specific term, the earlier one is *optionally* not treated as "non-existent" (avidyamāna-vat), and so *does not* lose its accent — hence the preceding vocative here keeps its accent, as being "not a pāda-beginning" (apādādi) it would otherwise take nighāta. **तत्र (*tatra*)** — "in that"; the *tral* suffix after the seventh-case pronouns *tad*, *kim*, *sarva* etc. (Pā. 5-3-10, "saptamyās tral"); *tral* is *taddhita*, so the word is a *prātipadika*; the *sup* ending is dropped by *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pā. 2-4-71); *d* → *a* by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. 6-2-102 [as printed]); *a* + *a* → pararūpa by *ato guṇe* (Pā. 6-1-97); *tral* is *l*-marked, so by *liti* (Pā. 6-1-193) the syllable before the suffix is udātta. **इन्द्र (*indra*)** — the second pāda's first syllable; since this is the beginning of the pāda, there is no lowering by *apādādau*; as a vocative it is initial-udātta by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. 6-1-198). **राये (*rāye*)** — *rai* + the dative ending *e*; after the *ai*-ending word *rai*, the dative ending is udātta (*ūḍidam-pada-ādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ*, Pā. 6-1-171). **रभस्वतः (*rabhasvataḥ*)** — root *rabha rābhasye*; *asun* by *sarvadhātubhyo 'sun* (Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]) gives *rabhas*, initial-udātta as *nit*; *matup* after it by *tad asyāsty asminn iti matup* (Pā. 5-2-94), its *m* → *v* by *mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-9); the question of whether *rabhas* is a *pada* before *matup* (which would block *ruṭ* etc.) (by *svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne*, Pā. 1-4-17) or has *bha* status (by *tasau matvarthe*, Pā. 1-4-19) is argued: *pada* status and *bha* status are both prescribed, and the source concludes by the maxim "ā kaḍārād ekā saṃjñā" (Pā. 1-4-1) that among the technical names prescribed from there up to *kaḍārāḥ karmadhāraye* (Pā. 2-2-38) only one applies, the later (*para*) one, *bha*; so *pada*-status is inapplicable and the rules (such as *ruṭv*-rules) that depend on it do not operate. **तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*)** — *tuvi* (much) + *dyumna* (wealth) as a bahuvrīhi; a vocative, initial-udātta by the vocative rule of the sixth adhyāya (no number printed). **यशस्वतः (*yaśasvataḥ*)** — "yaśo 'syāstīti yaśasvān": *matup*, with the *m* → *v* as in *rabhasvataḥ*; the long discussion (pp. 364–365) concerns whether the *vini* suffix of the sūtra "asmāyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121) blocks *matup* here — answered that, by the carried-over word "anyatarasyām" ("optionally"), *vini* is only optional — the "nityam" of *ekago-pūrvāṭ ṭhañ nityam* (Pā. 5-2-118) breaks the carrying-over, but it resumes in *tasau matvarthe* (Pā. 1-4-19), where the Mahābhāṣya gives the examples *yaśasvī / yaśasvān*; and by the Vedabhāṣya's general statement that *matup* has the sense of inclusion everywhere (*samuccaya*), and by Kaiyaṭa on the Mahābhāṣya on "keśād vo 'nyatarasyām" (Pā. 5-2-109; printed 5-3-109 on p. 365 [as printed]); *yaśas* is initial-udātta as a neuter noun not ending in *-isan* (Phiṭ-sūtra 26); *matup* is *pit*, hence unaccented; so the initial accent of *yaśas* stands. *(Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only.)*  ==>  **तत्र (*tatra*)** — "in that"; **गोमत्, वाजवत् (*gomat, vājavat*)** — "gaur asyāsti iti gomat; vājo 'sya asti iti vājavat": in both, *matup* is *pit*, hence unaccented, so the stem accent stands; *vāja* is a *vṛṣādi* word, so initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203). **अस्मे (*asme*)** — *asmad* + the dative-plural *bhyas*; this is replaced by *śe* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39); the *ś* of *śe* is *it* by "lasakvataddhite" (Pā. 1-3-8), the substitute being *śit* replaces the whole of *bhyas* by "anekāl śit sarvasya" (Pā. 1-1-55); *asmad* is final-udātta by its stem accent; [on the view that the *ṭi* is dropped,] the *e* is udātta by the accent of the lost udātta, "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161); [on the other view] the final *d* of *asmad* is dropped by "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-90); *asma* + *e* → *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), a single substitute that takes the udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). **पृथु (*pṛthu*)** — root *pṛtha prakhyāne* ("to spread"), and the rule "prathimradibhrasjāṃ saṃprasāraṇaṃ salopaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-28 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 366 prints 1-29): the suffix *ku* after *prath*, *mrad*, *bhrasj*, with *saṃprasāraṇa* of *r* to *ṛ* and loss of *s* in *bhrasj*; *pṛ* + *th* + *u* → *pṛthu* by the pūrvarūpa of "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108); *ku* is *kit*, so no *guṇa* by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86). **श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)** — "śrūyate iti": root *śru* + *asun* ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," no number printed); *guṇa* of *u* → *o* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84); *ov* → *av* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78); the nominative/accusative singular ending *am*/*su* dropped by "svamor napuṃsakāt" (Pā. 7-1-23); *ru*-and-visarga; initial-udātta. **बृहत् (*bṛhat*)** — stem accent. **विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)** — a bahuvrīhi "viśvam āyur yasmin dhane"; *viśva* + *āyuḥ* → single substitute *ā*, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). **अक्षितम् (*akṣitam*)** — root *kṣi kṣaye* in the sense including the causative; *kta* in the passive; by "niṣṭhā-yoṇya-darthe" (Pā. 6-4-60) the lengthening is prohibited since the word does not have the sense "not to be…"; the root *ṣidhu gatyām* (*ṣ* → *s* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ," Pā. 6-1-64); the prefix *nis*, in the sense of *ni*, stands before it; *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76), with all of *kvip* dropped; the *prādi* compound by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18). **The scholastic discussion (pp. 405–408):** between the *s* of the prefix *nis* and the root's *s* (here, *ṣidh*), the question is whether the *s* of *nis* "intervenes" (*vyavadhāna*) so that the retroflexion of the root's *s* by "upasargāt sunoti-suvati-syati-stauti-stobhati-sthā-senaya-sedha-sica-sañja-svañjām" (Pā. 8-3-65) is blocked — with "sahe sāḍaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 8-3-56), "apadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ" (Pā. 8-3-55) and "iṇkoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-57) carried over (p. 405); the *iṇ* of the prefix is taken as a qualifier by "yena vidhis tadantasya" (Pā. 1-1-72); the vārttika "upasargāt ṣatve niso upasaṃkhyānam aniṇantatvāt" (8-3-65 vārttika 1) and its rejoinder "na vā varṇāśrayatvāt" (8-3-65 vārttika 2) are cited; it is answered that by "numvisarjanīyaśarvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. 8-3-58) the intervention of *num*, *visarga* and *ś*, *ṣ*, *s* does not prevent the retroflexion, as the Mahābhāṣya says, "tatra śarvyavāye ity eva siddham"; the Vedabhāṣya's opinion that, because the intervention of the sibilant is "unobserved" in the Veda, the retroflexion arises, is discussed and is stated to be needless effort. "*Niṣ*" + "*ṣidh*": the *ṣ* is retained, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) the *s* of *nis* becomes *ṣ*, giving *niṣṣidh*; the compound with the genitive-dependent *puru* (*puru* is the object, "they bar many") gives *puruniṣṣidh* — a compound that, by "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139), keeps the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member. *Niṣṣidh* is a *kṛdanta* because *kvip* was added even though lost (by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam"; *kvip* comes only after a root, under the heading "dhātoḥ," Pā. 3-1-91); the long argument that the compound is formed with a verb-noun that is not itself a *kṛdanta* by the usual "kṛd-grahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" paribhāṣā (Paribhāṣā 28) settles that the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member stands. [sic]). **शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)** — "sphāyitañcivañciśaki…" (Uṇ. 2-170 [?] as printed, the second digit 7 or 2; the bhāṣya gives 2-13): the root *śakḷ śaktau* with *rak*; the accent by the suffix. **यथा (*yathā*)** — "prakāravacane thāl" (Pā. 5-3-23); Closing the grammar of **शकत् (*śakat*)**: by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43) the *cli* arises after the root (*śak* + *cli* + *t*); for the *cli* after a root of the *puṣādi*, *dyutādi*, and *ḷdit* classes in the parasmaipada, *aṅ* is substituted by "puṣādi-dyutādi-ḷditaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-1-55); the augment *aṭ* that "lūṅ-laṅ-lṛṅ-kṣv aḍudāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71) would give does not arise, by "bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi" (Pā. 6-4-75); wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **वसु (*vasu*)** — "śvā-svṛ-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-klidi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-10); *nit* is carried over from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. 1-9) and *uḥ* from "bhṛmṛśī…uḥ" (Uṇ. 1-7), so *u* comes after the ten roots *śvā* etc. and is *nit*; so *vasa nivāse* gives *vasu*, initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **दयमानः (*dayamānaḥ*)** — root *daya dāna-gati-rakṣaṇa-hiṃsā-dāneṣu*; *anudātta-it*, so ātmanepada by "anudātta-ṅita ātmanepadam" (printed "1-3-1" [as printed], i.e. 1-3-12); *śānac* for *laṭ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe" (Pā. 3-2-124); *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); before *āna* the short *a* of the stem takes the augment *muk* by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82), which is *kit* and so is added at the end ("ādyantau ṭakitau," Pā. 1-1-46): *day + a + mān + a*; *śap* is *pit* and so unaccented; the *śānac*, being *cit*, would give the final accent ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163), but since it follows *śap*, an *adupadeśa*, the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented (*tāsyanudāttenṅid-adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam*, Pā. 6-1-186), this is set aside and only the root's accent stands: *day*.  ==>  Closing the grammar of **शकत् (*śakat*)**: by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43) the *cli* arises after the root (*śak* + *cli* + *t*); **सुविवृतम् (*suvivṛtam*)** — root *vṛñ varaṇe* with *kta* in the passive; *vi* + *vṛta* are joined as *prādi*, and *su* with *vivṛta* as a further compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18); since *vṛta* is a *kṛdanta*, the rule "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the accent of the second member; this is set aside by "gatir anantaraḥ" (Pā. 6-2-49) (when a *kta*-ending word in the passive sense is the second member, a directly preceding *gati* keeps its own accent), so that the *vi* would be initial-udātta; this too is set aside by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199), making the first vowel (*ṛ*) of *vṛta* udātta. **The long argument (pp. 417–418):** when *su* is then compounded with *vivṛta*, "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" would again keep the accent of the second member, and that *ṛ* stays udātta. But the objection arises: in *su-vivṛta* is *vivṛta* a *kṛdanta*? — the paribhāṣā "pratyaya-grahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tad-ādes tad-antasya grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā 23) says that where a suffix is named, the item beginning with that to which it was added and ending in that suffix is meant; *vivṛta* is not *vṛta* alone — and the counter-paribhāṣā "kṛd-grahaṇe gati-kāraka-pūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā 28) says that a *kṛdanta* includes one preceded by a *gati* or a *kāraka*; hence *vivṛta* is a *kṛdanta*. A further difficulty (pp. 418): the sūtra "gatir anantaraḥ" with "anantara" ("immediately preceding") appears to bar the rule when something intervenes, as in *su-vi-vṛtam* where *vi* intervenes between *su* and *vṛta*; "kte ca" (printed "5-2-45" [as printed], i.e. 6-2-45) being carried into "gatir anantaraḥ", the answer is that, because of the word "anantara", the paribhāṣā "kṛd-grahaṇe…" is not present in that sūtra, and the counter-example *abhyuddhṛtam* (where the intervening *abhi* does not keep its own accent) is cited to show the use of the word *anantara*; the discussion concludes (p. 418) that in *suvivṛtam* the *ṛ* remains udātta. *(The page ends with "so ends this great-sentence discussion.")* **सुनिरजम् (*sunirajam*)** — the root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ* with the prefixes *su* and *nis*; "īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal" (Pā. 3-3-126) gives *khal* after a root when *īṣat*, *duḥ* or *su* is the *upapada*, in senses of difficulty/ease; the argument whether *nis* intervening between *su* and *aja* prevents the *khal* is answered: the rule does not require that the *su* stand immediately before (cf. *suparihāram*, *duṣparihāram*); *khal* is *l*-marked, so the vowel before it (*a* of *aj*) is udātta by "liti"; with the *gati*-compound with *nis*, the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member (the root's *a* udātta) stands; compounding again with *su* gives the same by Paribhāṣā 28; the remaining syllables are lowered; the unaccented *a* of the suffix becomes *svarita* by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (no number printed). **त्वादातम् (*tvādātam*)** — root *daip śodhane* — the argument on pp. 419–420: by "ādeca upadeśe 'śiti" (Pā. 6-1-45) the *e* of the root becomes *ā* when a non-*śit* suffix follows; but the root is *daip* ending in *p*, with *ai*, which in the *upadeśa* is a diphthong-ending root? — the difficulty is resolved by the paribhāṣā "nānubandhakṛtam anejantatvam" (Paribhāṣā 6) that the diphthong-ending status of a root is not undone by a mere *it*-marker; *kta* in the passive by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. 3-2-102), giving *dā* + *ta*; the objection that *dā* + *ta* would then be *ghu*-class and so take *dad* in place of *dā* ("dādhā ghv adāp," Pā. 1-1-20; "do dad ghoḥ," Pā. 7-4-46) is answered, since *dāp lavane* and *daip śodhane* are specifically excluded and the substitute-from-*daip* *dā* is "lākṣaṇika," not *pratipadokta*; the paribhāṣā "lakṣaṇa-pratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam" is argued and disposed of by "gāmādāgrahaṇeṣv aviśeṣaḥ" (Paribhāṣā 106). *Tvā* — *yuṣmad* + *ṭā*, the third-case ending replaced by *ā* via *ḍā* ("supāṃ suluk…" Pā. 7-1-39); *tva* replaces the part up to *m* of *yuṣmad* ("tvamāv ekavacane," printed "8-2-97" [as printed], i.e. 7-2-97), *tva* + *ad* + *a*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97); with *bha*-status the *ṭi* (*ad*) is dropped by "ṭeḥ" (Pā. 6-4-143), giving *tvā*; *yuṣmad* itself is from *yuṣ* with *madik* (Uṇ. 1-136); the *a* is udātta by "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161); the accent (pp. 420–421): the *ā* is udātta if a *prātipadika* accent applies; the third-case *tvā* compounds with the *kṛdanta* *dāta* by "kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-32); the ending of the third-case word would be dropped by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71) but is not dropped by "tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam" (Pā. 6-3-14); the *kṛdanta*'s second-member accent that would stand is set aside by "tṛtīyā karmaṇi" (Pā. 6-2-48): a third-case word followed by a *kta*-ending word in the passive sense keeps its own accent, so the first member's accent stands. **यशः (*yaśaḥ*)** — root *aśū vyāptau* + *asun* by "aśer yuṭ ca" (printed "pā. sū. 4-630" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 4-190), with the augment *yuṭ*; *yaśas*, with *su* dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68); *ru* and visarga; initial-udātta since the suffix is *nit*. **गवाम् (*gavām*)** — stem accent; *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca"; *śnu* by "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. 3-1-73), dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (2-4-73, printed "paṃ. sū." [sic]); after *śṛ*, *spṛ*, *kṛ*, *vṛ*, *bhṛ* in the Veda, *hi* → *dhi* ("śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi," Pā. 6-4-102); *hi* is *apit* so *ṅit*, hence no *guṇa* by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5); unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ". **कृणुष्व (*kṛṇuṣva*)** — root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*, *idit* so *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58), *num* being *mit* it stands after the last vowel ("mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ," Pā. 1-1-47); ātmanepada by inversion; *loṭ* with middle-second *thās* → *se* (Pā. 3-4-80), *se* → *sva* (Pā. 3-4-91); *kṛnv* + *sva*: the *śap* arising by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68) is set aside by "dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca" (Pā. 3-1-80): after *dhivi* and *kṛvi* — both *bhvādi* (first-class) roots, though Bopadeva takes them as *tanādi*, in whose view the *ca* of the sūtra is unnecessary — the *u*-vikaraṇa arises and the final of the root is changed to *a*, so *kṛṇ* + *u* + *sva* ("kṛn + a + u + sva"); **नहि (*nahi*)** — by "saha supā" (Pā. 2-1-4), a *subanta* compounds with a capable *subanta*, so *nañ* compounds with *hi*; being a compound, final-udātta by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223). **त्वा (*tvā*)** — *yuṣmad* + accusative singular *am*; by "ṅe prathamayor am" (Pā. 7-1-28) the *am* is replaced by *am*, so that the ending counts as a substitute and "yo 'ci" (Pā. 7-2-89, the *y*-substitute before a vowel-initial ending not causing *ā* or *y*) does not apply; "tvamāv ekavacane" (Pā. 7-2-97) gives *tva* for the part up to *m*: *tva* + *ad* + *am*; "dvitīyāyāṃ ca" (Pā. 7-2-87) gives *ā* before the accusative; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), *savarṇa-dīrgha* by "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-101), *pūrvarūpa* by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-107): *tvām*; then, under the headings "padasya", "padāt" and "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (8-1-18), "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ" (Pā. 8-1-23) gives the unaccented substitute *tvā* when not at the beginning of a pāda. **रोदसी (*rodasī*)** — root *rud* + *asun* ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]), *laghūpadha-guṇa*, *rodas*, initial-udātta since *nit*; the *u* of *asun* being *it*, *rodas* is *ugit*, so *ṅīp* in the feminine by "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6); *ṅīp* is *pit*, so unaccented. **उभे (*ubhe*)** — *ubha* is final-udātta by the stem accent; *ṭāp* by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (printed "8-1-4" [as printed], i.e. 4-1-4), unaccented as *pit*; *ubha* + *ā* → *savarṇa-dīrgha*, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ"; before the nominative/accusative dual *au*, "auṅa āpaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-18) gives *śī*, the *ś* dropped as *it*: *ubhā* + *ī*, the *ī* unaccented as a *sup*; "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-87) gives *e*, udātta as a single substitute. **ऋघायमाणम् (*ṛghāyamāṇam*)** — "nṝn hanti" ["he slays men"] gives *ṛghā* in the nominative singular: with *nṝn* as *upapada*, *han* takes *vic* by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. 3-2-75); all of *vic* drops; as a *kṛdanta* it is a *prātipadika*; the *śas* is dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71); the word "dṛśyante" in the sūtra serves to include other operations, so the *n* of *nṛ* is dropped and the *h* of *han* becomes *gh*: *ṛghan*. In the sense "becoming *ṛghā*, which one was not" (*abhūtatadbhāva*), *kyaṣ* by "lohitādiḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣ" (Pā. 3-1-13), the Lohitādi being an open (*ākṛti*) group; *k* and *ṣ* are *it*; with "lopaś ca halaḥ" carried from "bhṛśādibhyo bhuvy acver lopaś ca halaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-12), the final consonant is dropped; the *a* lengthened by "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (printed "7-8-35" [as printed], i.e. 7-4-25): *ṛghāya*; *laṭ*; by "vā kyaṣaḥ" (Pā. 1-3-90) the ātmanepada *śānac* ("laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau"); *śap*: *ṛghāya* + *a* + *āna*; *śap* is unaccented as *pit*, and the *śānac*, a *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* *śap*, is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. 6-1-186); *kyaṣ* has the suffix accent; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), the single substitute udātta; *muk* by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82), *n* → *ṇ*: *ṛghāyamāṇa*. *This derivation follows the Vṛttikāra; but in fact* kyaṣ *does not come here: the Lohitādi group contains only vowel-final words, and even as an open group* kyaṣ *does not come after a consonant-final word — the Mahābhāṣya on "lohitā…" says plainly "nāyaṃ halantād vidhīyate"; Kaiyaṭa, the Udyotakāra and the Kaumudī are cited in support, and the vārttika "lohitaḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣvacanam" with its rejection of the word ādi; there is also the Mahābhāṣya's separate denial for* n-*final words, "nāyaṃ nāntād vidhīyate". So the right derivation is: "ṛghā iva ācarati", with* kyaṅ *by "kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca" (Pā. 3-1-11) after a subanta denoting the standard of comparison and the agent: *ṛghan* + *su* + *ya*; as a *sanādi* form it is a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32), the *su* drops by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ"; by "naḥ kye" (Pā. 1-4-15) the *n*-final stem is a *pada* before *kyac*/*kyaṅ*, so the *n* drops by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7); since "nalopaḥ supsvarasaṃjñātugvidhiṣu kṛti" (Pā. 8-2-2) makes the loss "unseen" only for those rules, it is not unseen for lengthening ("pūrvatrāsiddham," Pā. 8-2-1), and "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-25) lengthens: *ṛghāya*; *kyaṅ* being *ṅit*, the ātmanepada by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (printed "1-3-1" [as printed], i.e. 1-3-12); the rest as above. **इन्वतः (*invataḥ*)** — root *ivi vyāptau*, *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58); In the sense "becoming *ṛghā*, which one was not" (*abhūtatadbhāva*), *kyaṣ* by "lohitādiḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣ" (Pā. 3-1-13), the Lohitādi being an open (*ākṛti*) group; *k* and *ṣ* are *it*; with "lopaś ca halaḥ" carried from "bhṛśādibhyo bhuvy acver lopaś ca halaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-12), the final consonant is dropped; the *a* lengthened by "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (printed "7-8-35", i.e. 7-4-25): *ṛghāya*; *laṭ*; by "vā kyaṣaḥ" (Pā. 1-3-90) the ātmanepada *śānac* ("laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau"); *śap*: *ṛghāya* + *a* + *āna*; *śap* is unaccented as *pit*, and the *śānac*, a *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* *śap*, is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. 6-1-186); *kyaṣ* has the suffix accent; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), the single substitute udātta; *muk* by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82), *n* → *ṇ*: *ṛghāyamāṇa*. *This derivation follows the Vṛttikāra; but in fact* kyaṣ *does not come here: the Lohitādi group contains only vowel-final words, and even as an open group* kyaṣ *does not come after a consonant-final word — the Mahābhāṣya on "lohitā…" says plainly "nāyaṃ halantād vidhīyate"; Kaiyaṭa, the Udyotakāra and the Kaumudī are cited in support, and the vārttika "lohitaḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣvacanam" with its rejection of the word ādi; there is also the Mahābhāṣya's separate denial for* n-*final words, "nāyaṃ nāntād vidhīyate". So the right derivation is: "ṛghā iva ācarati", with* kyaṅ *by "kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca" (Pā. 3-1-11) after a subanta denoting the standard of comparison and the agent: *ṛghan* + *su* + *ya*; as a *sanādi* form it is a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32), the *su* drops by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ"; by "naḥ kye" (Pā. 1-4-15) the *n*-final stem is a *pada* before *kyac*/*kyaṅ*, so the *n* drops by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7); since "nalopaḥ supsvarasaṃjñātugvidhiṣu kṛti" (Pā. 8-2-2) makes the loss "unseen" only for those rules, it is not unseen for lengthening ("pūrvatrāsiddham," Pā. 8-2-1), and "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-25) lengthens: *ṛghāya*; *kyaṅ* being *ṅit*, the ātmanepada by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (printed "1-3-1", i.e. 1-3-12); the rest as above. **इन्वतः (*invataḥ*)** — root *ivi vyāptau*, *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58); *laṭ* third dual *tas*; *śap*; *ru* and visarga; *śap* unaccented as *pit*; by "tāsyanudāttenṅid…" (Pā. 6-1-186) the *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* is unaccented, so the root accent stands; "hi ca" (Pā. 8-1-34), with "aprātilomye" carried from "aṅgāprātilomye" (Pā. 8-1-33) — *aprātilomya* means favourableness — forbids the lowering of a verb joined with *hi*, so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) does not apply. **जेषः (*jeṣaḥ*)** — root *ji jaye*; *leṭ* in the sense of *liṅ* (prayer); second singular *sip*, its *p* *it* by "halantyam" (Pā. 1-3-3); the *i* dropped by "itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-4-97); *śap* is set aside by "sibbahulaṃ leṭi" (Pā. 3-1-34): *ji* + *s* + *s*; the augment being unaccented, only the root accent stands. **स्वर्वतीः (*svarvatīḥ*)** — "svaḥ āsām asti": *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); its *m* → *v* by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. 8-2-15), *svar* ending in *r*, and also by "mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-9), *svar* having *a* as penultimate: *svarvat*; *ap* is *pit*, so unaccented; the accusative singular *am* with *pūrvarūpa* ("ami pūrvaḥ," printed "8-1-23" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-107), *havam*. **नु (*nu*)** — in the Saṃhitā the vowel is lengthened by "ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. 6-3-133), *nū*. **चित् (*cit*)** — belongs to the *cādi* class, so unaccented ("cādayo 'nudāttāḥ," Phiṭ-sūtra 84). **दधिष्व (*dadhiṣva*)** — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ* (*juhotyādi*); **विद्म (*vidma*)** — root *vida jñāne* ("to know") with *laṭ*; in the parasmaipada the first-person plural *mas*; *śap* is dropped by *luk* ("adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," Pā. 2-4-72); "vido laṭo vā" (Pā. 3-4-83): for the nine parasmaipada endings of *laṭ* after *vid* the substitutes *ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, ma* are optionally given, so *mas* → *ma*, giving *vidma*; **॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** The ṛṣi of the sūkta *indraṃ viśvā* is Jetā, son of the sage Madhucchandas. The Anukramaṇikā too says "*indram aṣṭau jetā mādhucchandasaḥ*" — that is, "of the [eight] riks *indraṃ viśvā*, the ṛṣi is Jetā, son of Madhucchandas." The meter, Anuṣṭubh, was stated earlier. The deity is Indra. Application: in the sacrifice called **Mahāvrata**, when reciting the mantras of the *niṣkevalya-śastra*, this whole sūkta is to be recited; Śaunaka says so in the section *ūrū* of the Śrauta-sūtra, and the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (5-2-1 [as printed]) gives the order of application of this sūkta, and the Brāhmaṇa-portion that explains it is in the same Āraṇyaka (1-5-2) in the section *pra vo mahe*. And on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya sacrifice, when reciting the *niṣkevalya-śastra*, the three riks beginning *indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan* are to be used for the *stomāvāpa*; Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra says so in the sūtra *upa no haribhiḥ sutam indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan*.  ==>  **॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** The ṛṣi of the sūkta *indraṃ viśvā* is Jetā, son of the sage Madhucchandas. Application: in the sacrifice called **Mahāvrata**, when reciting the mantras of the *niṣkevalya-śastra*, this whole sūkta is to be recited; Śaunaka says so in the section *ūrū* of the Śrauta-sūtra, and the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (5-2-1) gives the order of application of this sūkta, and the Brāhmaṇa-portion that explains it is in the same Āraṇyaka (1-5-2) in the section *pra vo mahe*. And on the fifth day of the Pṛṣṭhya sacrifice, when reciting the *niṣkevalya-śastra*, the three riks beginning *indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan* are to be used for the *stomāvāpa*; Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra says so in the sūtra *upa no haribhiḥ sutam indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan*.

**हृदिस्पृक् (*hṛdispṛk*)**: *hṛdi spṛśati iti hṛdispṛk*. By "spṛśo 'nudake kvin" (Pā. sū. 3-2-58), when a *subanta* other than the word *udaka* is the *upapada*, the suffix *kvin* comes after the root *spṛś*; all its letters drop. By "tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam" (Pā. sū. 6-3-14), when a *kṛdanta* final member follows, the locative in a *tatpuruṣa* compound is not dropped; so the *luk* due by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" does not come. After *hṛdispṛś* the suffix *su*, dropped by "halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68). The guttural enjoined by "kvinpratyayasya kuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-62) (in the *pada*-final position a word after which *kvin* came takes a guttural as its final substitute) counts as not done when the *ṣ* for a final *ś* is made by "vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrāja-cchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-36). So first *ṣ* comes by this sūtra: *spṛṣ*; then *jaś*, *ḍ* for *ṣ*, by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. sū. 8-2-39). By "naś cāpadāntasya jhali" (Pā. sū. 8-3-24) *anusvāra* for the *m*; by "anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-58), with the help of the *paribhāṣā* *sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ*, in place of the *anusvāra* comes *n*, homorganic with what follows and nasal: *gantṛ*. After it the nominative dual *au*; for it the substitute *ā* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39): *gantṛ* + *ā*. *Guṇa* by "ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-110), followed by *r* by *uraṇ raparaḥ*: *gantar* + *ā*. Here, by "ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-16), the *guṇa* enjoined for *ṛ*-final roots and *dṛś* comes when *aṅ* follows; here there is no suffix *aṅ*, so this sūtra does not apply. **पिपीषति (*pipīṣati*)**: the root *pā pāne*; analysed *pātum icchati*. "dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā" (Pā. sū. 3-1-7): the root *iṣu icchāyām*; after a root expressing an activity that has the same agent as this *iṣ* and is the object of the *iṣ*, the suffix *san* comes in the sense of wishing: that is the sense of the sūtra. Here the one who wishes is Agni; Agni is the agent of *iṣ*; the same Agni is the agent in the activity favourable to contact with the throat, which is the sense of *pā*; so the activity of *pā* has the same agent as the wishing, and this activity is the object of *iṣ*. So *san* comes after *pā*, denoting such an activity, in the sense of wishing: *pā* + *sa*; reduplication by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-9): *pā* + *pā* + *sa*; the reduplicate shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59); *i* for the *a* of the reduplicate by "sanyataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-79): *pipāsati*. Now the *ā* becomes *ī* as a Vedic form. *Ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59): *pipīṣati*. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" ("8-12-28" [as printed, for 8-1-28]).  ==>  **पिपीषति (*pipīṣati*)**: the root *pā pāne*; analysed *pātum icchati*. **दीद्यग्नी (*dīdyagnī*)**: the root *divu krīḍādau*; after it, by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. sū. 3-2-75) the suffixes *manin*, *kvanip*, *vanip* and *vic* come after roots; so *vic* after *div*: *div* + *v*. By "ver apṛktalopād vali lopo balīyān", the loss before *val* enjoined by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66) is stronger than the loss of the *v* enjoined by "ver apṛktasya" (Pā. sū. "6-1-62" [as printed, for 6-1-67]); so, though the *apṛkta* loss is *antaraṅga*, the first *v* drops first by "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66). On the view that the suffix drops first by "ver apṛktasya", by "varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam" (paribhāṣā "93-1" [?]), when an operation based on a letter is made, *pratyayalakṣaṇa* does not apply; so the following *val* could not be had, and the loss of the first *v* would not come. So first the first *v* drops as said, then the second *v* drops by "ver apṛktasya". As a Vedic form *di* is reduplicated: *didi*. Now by "tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-7) the first *di* is lengthened: *dīdi*. Or, after the root *div*, by "dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-22) *yaṅ*; by "yaṅo 'ci ca" (Pā. sū. 2-4-74) *yaṅ* takes *luk*; by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-9) reduplication: *div div*; by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-60) the *v* of the reduplicate goes: *didiv*. "guṇo yaṅlukoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-82): in *yaṅ* and in *yaṅluk* an *ik*-final reduplicate takes *guṇa*; so the first *di* would get *guṇa*. But by "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā "93-1" [?]) the *guṇa* rule is not binding, so it does not come here. "dīrgho 'kitaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-83): a vowel-final reduplicate that is not *kit* is lengthened in *yaṅ* and *yaṅluk*; so *dīdiv*. With *vic* as before, *dīdi*. *Dīdiḥ agniḥ yayoḥ tau dīdyagnī*, a bahuvrīhi compound. **शुचिव्रता (*śucivratā*)**: analysed *śuci vrataṃ yayoḥ tau*. By "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. "3-1-39" [as printed, for 7-1-39]) *ā* for the vocative-nominative dual. The two vocatives *dīdyagnī* and *śucivratā* are described as construed with *aśvinā*. So *aśvinā* is the general term,  ==>  **शुचिव्रता (*śucivratā*)**: analysed *śuci vrataṃ yayoḥ tau*. By "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. "3-1-39") *ā* for the vocative-nominative dual. The two vocatives *dīdyagnī* and *śucivratā* are described as construed with *aśvinā*. So *aśvinā* is the general term,

and the other two vocatives, being qualifiers, are themselves particular terms. So "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. sū. "8-1-23" [as printed, for 8-1-73]) has no scope. Since the two vocatives are not construed with each other, there is no connection of sense, so "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. "3-1-2" [as printed, for 2-1-2]) gives no joining as part of the following either. So the doubt rightly arises how the full lowering in *śucivratā* fits. But here we take *dīdyagnī* itself as the qualified, and say that *śucivratā* is its qualifier, and that this qualified pair is construed with *aśvinā*. Now *dīdyagnī* is a general term, so by "nāmantrite…" (Pā. sū. "8-1-23") the treatment as absent that "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. "8-1-62" [as printed, for 8-1-72]) would give is barred; so *śucivratā* is not at the head of the pāda, and by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19) it is wholly unaccented. Or, in this explanation, since *dīdyagnī* and *śucivratā* are construed with each other, there is a connection of sense, so by "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. sū. "3-1-2") the earlier is joined as part of the following; so the notion arises that *dīdyagnī śucivratā* is one word. So by the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) the first letter *dī* is initial udātta. Then by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. sū. On this view, since the *ā* and the loss of *n* enjoined by *sanaḥ ktici* are optional, it is fitting to explain that where they do not come the form *santi* is got. If the analysis *santyāṃ bhavaḥ* is meant, by "bhave chandasi" (Pā. sū. "4-41-10") the suffix *yat* comes in the Veda after the fitting locative of a stem in the sense of being; with *yat*, *santi* + *ṅi* + *ya*. Or if the analysis *santyāṃ sādhuḥ* is made, by "tatra sādhuḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-4-98) *yat* in the sense *sādhu* after the fitting locative; with *yat*, *santi* + *ṅi* + *ya*. In both places the *sup* inside the *taddhita*-ending stem takes *luk*. By "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the *i* drops: *santya*. Nominative singular *santyaḥ*, vocative singular *santya*. Wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19).

*kvip* drops; *s* for *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64). The *am*, a *sup* inside the *kṛdanta* *prātipadika*, takes *luk*: *ghṛtasnu*. Now, though the *kvip*, a *pit* *kṛt*, has dropped, by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-62) it counts as following; so the augment *tuk* would come by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk". But by a Vedic process it does not come; or it does not come by "āgamaśāstram anityam" (paribhāṣā 94). *Snu* being a root, it is final udātta by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162); after compounding too, by the *kṛt* second-member accent of "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) that accent remains. After *ghṛtasnu*, *śas*: *ghṛtasnu* + *as*; the *u* stands after the conjunct *sn*. So by "oḥ supi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-83), before a vowel-initial *sup*, a stem of several vowels ending in a root that ends in *u*, not preceded by a conjunct belonging to the root itself, takes *yaṇ*: so *yaṇ* does not come. By "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. "6-9-22" [as printed, for 6-4-77]) *uvaṅ* for the *u*: *ghṛtasnuvam*.  ==>  *kvip* drops; *s* for *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64). **प्रयति (*prayati*)**: the root *iṇ gatau*, *adādi*; after it *laṭ*; in its place, by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) *śatṛ*; the *śap* that comes by "kartari śap" takes *luk* by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72): *i* + *at*. By "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) the suffix *at* is *ṅit*; so the *guṇa* that "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" would give is barred by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5). "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) would give *yaṇ*; overriding it, "aci śnudhātubhruvām…" (Pā. sū. "6-4-22" [as printed, for 6-4-77]) would give *iyaṅ*; overriding that too, "iṇo yaṇ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-81): before a vowel-initial suffix the root *iṇ* takes *yaṇ*; so *yaṇ*: *yat*. By "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18) *pra* is compounded with it: *prayat*; locative singular *ṅi*: *prayati*. The suffix *śatṛ* is udātta by the suffix accent; after compounding too, by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* the *kṛt* second-member accent comes and that accent remains. So *prayat* is final udātta; so by "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. sū. 6-1-173), after a final-udātta word ending in a *śatṛ* suffix without the augment *num*, a *nadī* letter and a vowel-initial ending from *śas* on are also udātta; so the locative singular *ṅi* becomes udātta. But how does *prayat*, *a*, end in the *śatṛ* suffix? By "pratyayagrahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tadādes tadantasya grahaṇam" (paribhāṣā 23), the word with the *śatṛ* suffix whose first member is the base and whose last member is *śatṛ* is the *śatṛ*-ending word. Here *śatṛ* is enjoined after the root *iṇ*, so *yat* ends in *śatṛ*, but *prayat* does not. So how does the ending get udātta? Thus: *śatṛ* is a *kṛt* suffix; so by "kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" (paribhāṣā 28), where the *kṛt* is named with the property of being *kṛt*, which pervades it, there forms with a *gati* or *kāraka* before them are taken too: so this paribhāṣā tells.  ==>  **प्रयति (*prayati*)**: the root *iṇ gatau*, *adādi*; after it *laṭ*; in its place, by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) *śatṛ*; the *śap* that comes by "kartari śap" takes *luk* by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72): *i* + *at*. By "ṅiti hrasvaś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-6), before a *ṅit* suffix, the *ī*/*ū*-final words that are fit for *iyaṅ*/*uvaṅ*, other than *strī*, that always denote the feminine, and the short *i*/*u*-final words denoting the feminine, are optionally called *nadī*; since the *nadī* name is optional, on the view where it does not come, by "śeṣo ghy asakhi" (Pā. sū. 1-4-7) the *ghi* name comes. **सवनम् (*savanam*)**: meant as "*sūyate asmin somaḥ*", in it the soma is pressed: the root *ṣūñ prāṇiprasave*; *s* for *ṣ* by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*; after *sū*, in the sense of place, *lyuṭ* by "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-117); the substitute *ana* by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1): *sū* + *ana*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-44 [as printed, for 7-3-84]); the substitute *av* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): *savana*. The *a* before the suffix *ana* is udātta by "liti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-193). *Savana* is a *lyuḍanta* in the sense of place. After it comes the locative singular suffix *ṅi*.  ==>  **सवनम् (*savanam*)**: meant as "*sūyate asmin somaḥ*", in it the soma is pressed: the root *ṣūñ prāṇiprasave*; *s* for *ṣ* by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*; after *sū*, in the sense of place, *lyuṭ* by "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-117); the substitute *ana* by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1): *sū* + *ana*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-44); the substitute *av* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): *savana*. In its place, by "supāṃ supo bhavanti" (Pā. sū. Vā. 3-1-39-1 [as printed; the vārttika is on 7-1-39]), stated in the sūtra "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) (in place of *sup* endings the intended *sup* endings come), the accusative singular *am* comes. *Savana* + *am*: by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) the *pūrvarūpa*: *savanam*. *Savane sutam idaṃ piba*: in this alternative the sense is "O Indra, drink the soma pressed in the rite in the form of the morning pressing and so on". Or, meant as "*sutam asya asti*", by "arśaādibhyo 'c" (Pā. sū. 5-2-127) the suffix *ac*: *suta* + *a*; by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the *a* is dropped. *Sutam* means "joined with the pressed soma juice". In this alternative *sutam idaṃ savanaṃ piba* means "enjoy this rite of the morning pressing and so on, joined with the pressed soma juice". Since *savana* denotes the object marked by the action conveyed by the root *pā*, the justification can be given that the accusative comes by "karmaṇi dvitīyā" (Pā. sū. 2-9-2 [as read; for 2-3-2] [?]). In the Vedabhāṣya, explaining the sense, *savanam* is taken as a nominative and the verb is supplied; in that alternative it must be said that *am* is substituted for the nominative singular suffix by *supāṃ suluk*.  ==>  In its place, by "supāṃ supo bhavanti" (Pā. sū. **अण्वीभिः (aṇvībhiḥ)** — This word, which ends in the instrumental plural, is used only in this Ṛk. *(The print says "caturthī-bahuvacana-anta"— "ending in the dative plural" — but "-bhiḥ" is the instrumental plural; this is evidently a slip in the source and is recorded here, not corrected silently.)* Among the twenty-two words that denote "aṅguli" (finger), the word "aṇvī" is read (Nighaṇṭu 2-5 [print: "ni. 2-5"]). The Bhāṣyakāra and the others also all explain this word as "fingers." Because the word is derived from "aṇu" (very small, fine), some think that the word means "a cloth with many fine openings — a net — used to strain the Soma." But when the Soma creeper is crushed with the stones (grāvāṇa), fingers must be used in straining it; so to say "aṇvībhiḥ sutāḥ" — "the juice extracted with the fingers" — is right. Moreover, since "pūtāsaḥ" already carries the sense "purified," "purified with fingers" and "purified with a net-like cloth" are equally fitting. This is why some accept the sense "with a net-like cloth" for "aṇvībhiḥ." **Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept):** "Uta" — a particle, first-syllable acute (**निपाता आद्युदात्ताः**, Phiṭ-sūtra 4-14). "Subhagān" — "bhaga" ends, in the "kṛtvādi" class, with the first member's accent set aside: **नञ्सुभ्याम्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) would give the end-acute, but "bhaga" is read in the list beginning with "kṛtva" — **क्रत्वादयश्च** (पा. सू. ६-२-११८) — so the second member is first-syllable acute. In the saṃhitā: **दीर्घादटि समानपादे** (पा. सू. ८-३-९) the "n" of "subhagān" becomes "ru" before a vowel; **भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि** (पा. सू. ८-३-१७) the "y"; **लोपः शाकल्यस्य** (पा. सू. ८-३-१९) the "y" is elided; since the elision is "asiddha," no further sandhi occurs; **आतोऽटि नित्यम्** (पा. सू. ८-३-३) the "ā" takes the nasal sign. "Ariḥ" — "vacana-vyatyaya" (a change of number: singular for plural); from "ṛ" with the Uṇādi "i" (**अर्त्तेरिः**, उ. सू. ४-१३७; printed "4-578") with the end-acute by the accent of the affix. "Vocēyuḥ" — "ucyāsuḥ": the root "vac" (to speak) in the benedictive (āśīrliṅ), "jhi → jus" (**झेर्जुस्**, पा. सू. ३-४-१०८); "liṅ" = "yāsuṭ" (**लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य**, पा. सू. ७-२-७९); the "ṅit" "yāsuṭ" is acute by **यासुट् परस्मैपदेषूदात्तो ङिच्च** (पा. सू. ३-४-१०३); the "ṅit" bars guṇa and, by **वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति** (पा. सू. ६-१-१५), the "samprasāraṇa" → "uc"; by Vedic **छन्दस्युभयथा** (पा. सू. ३-४-११७) the augment "āṭ" is absent; "s" is elided (**लोपोऽनन्त्यस्य**, as printed); the accents conflict, the "e" of the "yāsuṭ" being the single substitute of "a + ī" is acute (**एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः**, पा. सू. ८-२-५). **शतक्रतो (śatakrato)** — The Bhāṣyakāra explains this word as "bahukarmayukta" — one who does many daring deeds. **Veṅkaṭamādhava** has explained the word "kratu" as "prajñā" (wisdom). **Skandasvāmī** has given both of these senses. Here the word "śata" is used in the sense "many." In English also it is the custom to use the words "hundred" and "thousand" *(English as printed)* in the sense of "many." In the Purāṇas and other works the word "śatakratu" has the sense "one who has performed a hundred Aśvamedha sacrifices"; and, since it is well known that Indra, before obtaining the rank of Indra, performed a hundred Aśvamedha sacrifices and attained that rank, and that those who perform a hundred sacrifices obtain the rank of Indra, it is said in the Purāṇas and elsewhere that in many contexts Indra causes many obstacles, so that others may not perform a hundred sacrifices. But Indra's place in the Vedas is different, and his place as stated in the Purāṇas and later works is different. That is: in the Vedas Indra is praised as the foremost and most excellent among the gods, and there are many sūktas that praise his daring deeds. Why so? In the Ṛgveda the praises of Indra are as many as those of any other deity; in the Purāṇas and later works, the place of Indra is described as a lower place, subject to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the other deities. **The argument about the two "ā"s.** The print then asks how the single verb "ita" can be construed with *two* prefixes "ā … ā." The two prefixes, it says, are meant to be understood as one doubled prefix (**आदरार्थोऽभ्यासः**, "the doubling is for respect"). The text argues: if the two "ā"s were joined with one "ita" at the same time, the sense would be of two separate prefixing operations on one verb, which is not possible, because a single verb-action cannot be joined at once with two identical prefixes; so one "ā" joins "ita," and the other "ā" needs its own verb. > **Translation, in outline:** "…and going in every direction. Who (engages him)? By capacity, charioteers such as Mātali; others yoke his chariot; 'he himself yokes us' — one endowed with 'bradhna' and other qualities; they yoke nothing (else) (?). Thus this is praise of Indra by the proclaiming of his qualities. Further: 'tasthuṣaḥ rocante rocanā divi' — by the genitive 'tasthuṣaḥ' the supplied word is 'by the power': by the power of Indra, who is stationed and active, 'rocante' — shine; 'rocanā' — the stars, whose nature is shining, 'divi' — in heaven. How, then, do the stars shine by Indra's power? It will be said: '*Indra made the Sun rise in heaven for long sight*' (a quotation, as printed). The Sun's power is the ray called Suṣumna, and by connection with it the Moon and stars shine. Or else the root 'yuj' has the sense 'ut-' ('up'): it must be understood with the causal sense included — 'they urge up, they stir up Indra, great and ruddy, to the rain-work.' Doing what? 'Carantam pari tasthuṣaḥ' — 'pari' is a karmapravacanīya in the sense of 'around' and is connected with 'tasthuṣaḥ' — the word means 'the stationary': going toward the stationary; the mention of the stationary here is also to show the moving ones: moving around the whole world of moving and stationary beings, out of eagerness for the battle with the Asuras, for the Soma-drinking. Who stir him up? — 'rocante rocanā divi': for the unity of the sentence 'yat' and 'tat' must be supplied: the Sun's rays shine in heaven; those rays, at the beginning of the rainy season, take up the juices; offering those juices, they stir Indra to the rain-work. (Grammatical remarks on the neuter 'rocanā' follow.) … But the Adhvaryus regard the Ṛk as having the Sun for its deity. How? 'For in the application of these (mantras) the yoked horse is spoken of in the form of the Sun.' How is that known? **स्वधाम् (svadhām)** — Among the twenty-eight words that signify food, beginning with "andha," the words "ūrk," "rasaḥ" and "svadhā" are read (Ni. 2-7), and among the 101 words that signify water beginning with "arṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ" the word "svadhā" is also read (Ni. 1-12). > हे इन्द्र श्रवो धनमस्मे सं धेहि । अस्मभ्यं सम्यक् प्रयच्छ । कीदृशं श्रवः । गोमत् बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेतं वाजवत् प्रभूतेनान्नेनोपेतं पृथु परिमाणेनाधिकं बृहत् गुणैरधिकं विश्वायुः कृत्स्नायुष्यकारणं अक्षितं विनाशरहितम् । गोमत् । वाजवत् । उभयत्र मतुपो ऽनुदात्तत्वात्प्रातिपदिकस्वर एव । वाजशब्दो वृषादिराद्युदात्तः । अस्मे । अस्मच्छब्दाच्चतुर्थीबहुवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना शे आदेशः । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । शेषे लोपः । टिलोप इति पक्षे । पा. सू. ७-२-९० । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अन्त्यलोपपक्षे ऽतो गुण इति पररूपे एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तत्वम् । पृथु । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथिम्रदिभ्रस्जां संप्रसारणं सलोपश्च । उ. सू. १-२९ । इति कुप्रत्ययः । रेफस्य संप्रसारणमृकारः । परपूर्वत्वम् । कोः कित्त्वान्न लघूपधगुणः । श्रूयत इति श्रवो धनम् । असुन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । बृहत् । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । विश्वायुः । विश्वमायुर्यस्मिन्धने । विश्वशब्दः क्वन्प्रत्ययान्तः । तस्य बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्याद्युदात्तः । अक्षितम् । क्षि क्षये इत्यस्मादन्तर्णीतण्यर्थात्कर्मणि निष्ठा । तेन स्यदर्थत्वान्निष्ठायामण्यदर्थे [? **"Śravaḥ"** — for this word Yāska, in his Nirukta, gives two or three different senses. Since the word *śravaḥ* is read among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with *magham* and *reknaḥ* (Nirukta 3-9), the sense "wealth" is also possible. In explaining the rik *uta svainaṃ* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4-38-5) he says: "*śravaś cāpi paśum ucche yūthaṃ praśaṃsāṃ ca yūthaṃ dhanaṃ ca yūthaṃ ceti vā*" (as printed) — that is, *śravaḥ* is "praise (fame)" or "wealth" (Nirukta 4-24); and in the rik *amandān stomān* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-126-1; the first digit of the middle number is damaged in the print) he explains the word *śrava icchamānāḥ* as "wishing for praise" (Nirukta 9-11). In the explanation of the rik *pra vo mahe mandamānāya* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-50-1) he explains *śravaḥ* as *mahac chravaṇīyaṃ yaśaḥ* — "great, worthy-of-hearing glory" (Nirukta 11-10). Since in this rik, besides this, the word *dyumnam* ("wealth") also occurs — a word for wealth — to render *śravaḥ* as "wealth" would produce the fault of repetition; so to give it the sense of "fame" is quite fitting.  ==>  **"Śravaḥ"** — for this word Yāska, in his Nirukta, gives two or three different senses. **Translation:** "The *rātayaḥ* — gifts of wealth — of Indra are *pūrvīḥ*: established from beginningless time, or abundant. The sense: to give wealth to those who sacrifice is always this Indra's very nature. This being so, if even the present-day sacrificer gives to the *stotṛs*, the priests, as sacrificial fee, *magham* — sufficient wealth — of *vāja*, food, accompanied by cows, then Indra's *ūtayaḥ* — protections, preceded by many gifts of wealth — directed to us *na vi dasyanti*, are not specially diminished. Among the twenty-eight words for 'wealth' beginning with *magham* and *rekṇaḥ*, *magha* is read; among the ten words for acts of giving beginning with *dāti*, *dāśati*, *maṃhate* is read."
